subject: Gateway auth flags mislabeling — urgent: NimbusPay 5xx/429 surge
messages:
From: Grace Liu <ops@nimbuspay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood — urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sharp rise in downstream 5xx and 429 responses against the /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings endpoints around 08:50 PT this morning. Latency jumped from ~120ms to >1s for many requests; retries from our side spiked and cascaded.

Attached is a short sample (nimbus_error_sample.log) and some request IDs — several of the failures look like token validation errors in the gateway (we're on JWT short-lived tokens). We haven't rotated keys.

We're in production traffic for a scheduled batch and this is impacting live payments. Can you triage immediately and advise whether we should pause traffic?

- Grace
Ops, NimbusPay

Attachments: nimbus_error_sample.log (text), request_traces_0914.zip (zip)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Hi Grace — thanks for the samples, and sorry for the interruption. We're triaging now.

Immediate plan:
- Marcus/Monica are pulling gateway traces for the request IDs you shared.
- Can you confirm the system clocks on your token issuer /auth server? Any drift or recent NTP changes?
- If you can throttle non-critical batches we can put an emergency routing policy in place to divert to a tolerant model variant while we root-cause.

I'll circle back in 20 minutes with an update.

Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:53:00 -0700
Subject: FW: traces + quick findings

FYI — quick engineering note after an initial pass on the traces Grace sent.

Observations:
- Multiple failures are being produced by the auth/gateway layer returning 401/403 at the JWT validation step, but our edge layer is mapping some of them incorrectly to 429 and 5xx when certain downstream cache lookups fail.
- Root cause candidate: clock skew between NimbusPay's token issuer and our gateway causes tokens to be considered "not yet valid" (nbf) intermittently. Our policy for handling nbf tokens currently falls back into a retryable error path for a subset of front-door proxies which escalates to 429/502s in some client SDKs.
- We also saw ~2% of requests showing malformed keyid (kid) metadata that triggered a short-lived cache miss which our gateway treated as transient and retried, amplifying load.

Immediate mitigation suggestion (low-risk, minutes):
1) Apply an auth-layer mapping change to surface nbf/exp validation failures as 401 with clear error code rather than 429/5xx.
2) Bypass the cache miss fallback for kid lookup for 10 minutes (force fetch JWKs) while we reconcile key rotation.
3) Put NimbusPay on a temporary route with higher concurrency limits to reduce client-side retries (we will cap parallelism and instruct their SDKs to back off).

I'll start the mapping change now but will need Monica to approve the config rollback window.

-marcus
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: traces + quick findings

Approve the mapping change and forced JWK refetch. 15-minute safe window; monitor SLIs and be ready to rollback. Marcus — coordinate with edge ops to push the config (edge-config v3.12) and add verbose logging for auth failures.

Kimberly — I'll prepare a short client-facing note to NimbusPay explaining the temporary routing and asking them to throttle non-essential batches. Also open an incident ticket and loop Aditya for exec escalation if Grace reports customer impact beyond the batch window.

Monica Patel
Head, Customer Reliability

From: Grace Liu <ops@nimbuspay.com>

Subject: Re: Gateway auth flags mislabeling — update and follow-up

Thanks for the quick turnaround — the temporary mapping change and forced JWK refetch eliminated the 5xx/429 surge for our batch window. We reverted our internal retry aggressors and traffic returned to nominal latency by ~11:15 PT.

Follow-ups we need together:
- Nimbus will schedule a key rotation sanity check and confirm NTP sync across our auth fleet.
- Can Redwood provide a short postmortem that explains the mapping logic and the plan to make auth validation non-retryable (permanent fix)?
- Also asking for a modest credit for the impacted batch — will pass details to Kimberly.

Grace Liu
Ops, NimbusPay
